## Result — full analysis executed (all three locked decisions honoured)

**Deliverables (executed / written to workspace):**
- `analysis/meta_regression_analysis.py` — executed twice, deterministic (seeded bootstrap), non-empty output
- `analysis/summary_table.csv` — 6 rows × 44 cols; per group: n, n_tiny_n, n_tiny_n_in_ee, mean/median d_fz + t-CI + 10k bootstrap CI, paired-t p, Wilcoxon p, %ro>rr + Clopper-Pearson CI, **IV-weighted d_fz + 95% CI**, trimmed-run estimates (unweighted & IV), median relative_es (raw / trimmed / |ro|>0.2), replicated rate, mean no/nr/power
- `analysis/results_log.txt` (full log), `analysis/hypothesis.md` (final hypothesis), `analysis/inspection_report.py`

### FINAL HYPOTHESIS
> **Original studies report larger effects than their replications in all three domains present in this data — Social psychology, Cognitive psychology and Economics — so no domain is exempt; what differs is how robust the gap is. The most consistent domain is Social psychology (ro > rr in 88.2% of its 34 studies, mean Fisher-z gap 0.233 [0.162, 0.304], paired p = 1.3e-07, and by far the largest proportional shrinkage: median replication/original ratio 0.131 vs 0.650 Cognitive and 0.698 Economics; only 20.6% of Social replications "replicated" vs 47.1% Cognitive and 61.1% Economics). Cognitive psychology has the largest per-study gap (0.289 [0.164, 0.415], 82.4% of studies, p = 4.5e-05). Economics — note that in these data the Economics domain IS the Experimental Economics project, discipline being perfectly nested in project, so a domain claim is simultaneously a project claim — also tends to favour originals at the study level (0.266 [0.084, 0.447], 83.3% of its 18 studies, p = 0.0067, Wilcoxon p = 0.00084), but that gap is weighting-dependent and NOT robust: precision-weighted it collapses to 0.013 [-0.052, 0.078] versus 0.208 [0.161, 0.255] Social and 0.206 [0.132, 0.279] Cognitive (Social − Economics +0.195 [0.086, 0.304] p = 0.0006; Cognitive − Economics +0.193 [0.060, 0.325] p = 0.0050; discipline Wald F(2) = 7.03, p = 0.0015). The Economics pattern is not driven by tiny originals (only 2 of the 5 studies with no < 10 are Experimental Economics; dropping all no < 10 and |ro| < 0.2 leaves EE at 0.190 [0.063, 0.316], 85.7% ro > rr, paired p = 0.0065), but within EE the gap shrinks systematically with sample size (correlation with replication SE = +0.65; mean gap 0.436 in the low replication-N half vs 0.096 in the high-N half), so well-powered economics replications reproduce the original effect nearly exactly while underpowered ones do not. At the project level, Psychology (0.261 [0.191, 0.332], 85.3%) and Experimental Economics (0.266 [0.084, 0.447], 83.3%) are indistinguishable on the primary unweighted scale (difference +0.004, p = 0.96; Mann-Whitney p = 0.28) and differ only after precision weighting (IV difference −0.194, p = 0.0003, exploratory).**

Extra diagnostics requested: **tiny-N (no<10): 5 studies, 2 of them EE** (Chen & Chen 2011 d=1.058; Duffy & Puzzello 2014 d=1.116; other 3 Cognitive). EE trimmed (n=14) unweighted 0.190 [0.063,0.316], p=0.0065 → unweighted EE gap robust to trimming; its IV collapse is not. Unweighted HC3 regression shows **no domain difference** (Social−Econ −0.033 p=0.73; Cognitive−Econ +0.024 p=0.83) — hence the headline is "larger in originals in every domain", with the precision-weighted divergence reported rather than suppressed. Bootstrap CIs match t-CIs within ±0.001; |ro|>|rr| share identical to signed share (all ro>0).

### Assumptions
- Primary scale = unweighted study-level mean/median of d = fiso − fisr; IV pooled estimate reported with equal prominence as sensitivity.
- Domain grain = discipline primary, project secondary; Economics equated explicitly with the Experimental Economics project in the wording.
- relative_es (rr/ro) used only as sensitivity (median, trimmed, |ro|>0.2); no hard exclusions in the primary analysis.
- File used as-is (86 unique studies, 0 duplicates, 0 missing effect values); n.r, aggregated, lab_id, pm_belief unused; post-hoc power descriptive only.
- Pre-registered family (3 discipline paired tests + between-discipline meta-regression) Holm-adjusted; project-level comparisons labelled exploratory.

### Limitations
- n=18 in Economics → wide intervals; the weighting-dependence claim rests on few large-N studies.
- Discipline is perfectly nested in project (Cognitive/Social exist only in Psychology), so domain cannot be separated from project/site effects; domain differences co-vary with replication power (mean power.r 0.285 Social vs 0.726 Economics), so the IV-weighted domain contrast partly measures who ran bigger replications.
- Only 2 projects / one cohort of replication attempts; no correction across the exploratory project, trimmed and relative_es family; IV weights assume the analytic SEs (verified = 1/sqrt(n−3)) are correct.

payload.workflow: Loaded the joined CSV as-is (86 studies, 0 duplicates, 0 missing effect values; aggregated/lab_id/n.r/pm_belief unused). Built per-study paired difference d = fiso - fisr with SE_pair = sqrt(se_fiso^2 + se_fisr^2). PRIMARY scale = unweighted study-level tendency per domain (mean/median d, t-based CI, 10k seeded bootstrap CI, paired t-test, Wilcoxon, %ro>rr with Clopper-Pearson CI) for the three disciplines (primary grain) and both projects (secondary/exploratory). Equally prominent sensitivity: inverse-variance weighted pooled estimate per group plus IV-weighted meta-regression d ~ 1 + Social + Cognitive (ref = Economics) with joint Wald test, and a matching unweighted HC3 OLS. Sensitivity runs: trimmed (no<10 and |ro|<0.2 removed) for every estimator, tiny-N composition by project, gap-vs-precision correlations and EE median-N split, and relative_es = rr/ro (median, trimmed, |ro|>0.2). Holm correction over the pre-registered family (3 discipline paired tests + meta-regression); project-level comparisons flagged exploratory. Results written to analysis/summary_table.csv and analysis/results_log.txt; hypothesis in analysis/hypothesis.md.
